When Denis Villeneuve hit the scene with PRISONERS, who could have known he’d eventually be whispering to sand worms and communing with the desert on the biggest cinematic scale imaginable?

Nearly two decades after Paul Atreides (Timothée Chalamet) seized control of the Imperium, the bill for all that power has finally come due. Reunited with Chani and haunted by visions of collapse, Paul faces rebellion, betrayal, terrifying new enemies, and the unsettling possibility that we should have stopped rooting for innocent little Paul Atreides a long time ago. Zendaya caps her third blockbuster of 2026 with an epic finale that demands the biggest screen you can find.

show.headline: Mind the house rules

event.title: <show-title>Littermates</show-title> <event-type-title>Advance Screening</event-type-title>
event.headline: Catch the latest Alamo Exclusives film early
event.description:
Q&A to follow in DTLA

At Chester’s cottage, good behavior earns karaoke. Getting answers is a little more complicated.

After a mysterious apocalyptic(ish) attack leaves them bloodied, disoriented, and unable to speak, Liam (Joey Bader) and Mel (Kaylee McGregor) take refuge in the English countryside. Their oddball host, Chester (Oliver Woolf), feeds them, helps them recover, and introduces a system of rewards: behave yourself, earn “nifties,” cash them in for hot-tub time and dance parties.

Beyond the cottage, things are less nifty. But within it, a makeshift family is taking shape. While Liam embraces their new life, Mel grows increasingly curious about the world Chester insists is too dangerous to enter…

In their feature debut, directors Scott Tinkham and Michael Woloson mix deadpan comedy, sibling rivalry, and creeping unease in a coming-of-age story about people who have to grow up all over again. Winner of the Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Manchester Film Festival and the Narrative Feature Audience Award at Dances With Films LA 2026, this has the sort of sensibilities that fans of Yorgos Lanthimos and Ben Wheatley will adore… and it’s a natural fit as an Alamo Exclusive.

show.title: Daughters of Darkness
show.headline: They are waiting for you...they thrive on blood!

event.title: <show-title>Daughters of Darkness</show-title>
event.headline: Delphine Seyrig dazzles in this 1970s erotic lesbian vampire cult classic
event.description:
"I'm just an outmoded character, nothing more. You know, the beautiful stranger, slightly sad, slightly… mysterious… that haunts one place after another."

In the early 1970s, hardboiled crime films were all the rage: CHINATOWN, THE GODFATHER, THE FRENCH CONNECTION dominated the cineplex across the country. But simultaneously, there was another genre on the rise: the erotic lesbian vampire film. From THE VAMPIRE LOVERS to SHIVER OF THE VAMPIRES to VAMPYRES (which you know is queer because of its unconventional spelling), the era was riddled with attempts to cash in on the new lezzie blood-sucking craze. A standout from the red deluge of immortal sapphic stories was DAUGHTERS OF DARKNESS, a French, Belgian, and German collaboration helmed by Harry Kümel. When chaotic newlywed couple Valerie (Danielle Ouimet) and Stefan (John Karlen) arrive at a grand hotel on the Ostend seafront during the off-season, they initially seem to be the only guests in residence. That is, until the glamorous and preternaturally youthful Hungarian countess Elizabeth Báthory (Delphine Seyrig) arrives with her icy secretary Ilona (Andrea Rau). The Countess quickly becomes fixated on Valerie, and the dubious honeymoon is thrown into bizarre and erotic disarray.

Featuring an incredible and funky score by François de Roubaix and stunning decadent garments, DAUGHTERS OF DARKNESS is a vibe, and it’s so queeeeer. Decadent, alluring, dreamy, and strange, we can’t wait to watch this gorgeous film with you on the big screen as part of Queer Film Theory 10. Come, glamorous darlings, haunt us with your startling visage.

show.headline: Every family has its dark secrets

event.title: <show-title>A Tale of Two Sisters</show-title>
event.headline: Sad Girl Cinema Club gets spooky with Kim Jee-woon’s top tier twisted tale
event.description:
A TALE OF TWO SISTERS begins with Su-mi’s (Im Soo-jung) return home from her time away at a mental institution, and her homecoming is less than ideal. Her heavily medicated stepmother Eun-joo (Yum Jung-ah) rules the house, erratic and violent, she often terrified her younger sister Su-yeon (Moon Geun-young). However, their stepmother is not the only one wreaking havoc in their home: the ghost of their mother also haunts them in the evenings, fragmenting the barrier between what is real and what is psychosis.

Korean New Wave spearhead Kim Jee-woon’s diabolical fairy tale is filled with twists and turns. A TALE OF TWO SISTERS is an achingly haunted tale of sisterhood, evil stepmothers, and deadbeat dads. A luscious slow burn, the film to this day remains one of the most affecting Korean horror films of all time.

What is girlhood without a little bit of insanity?

event.title: <show-title>The Hole (1998)</show-title>
event.headline: Tsai Ming-Liang's surrealist fantasy musical, new 35mm print!
event.description:
In Mandarin with English subtitles

Set just prior to the start of the 21st century, this vaguely futuristic story follows two residents of a quickly crumbling building who refuse to leave their homes in spite of a virus that has forced the evacuation of the area. As rain pours down relentlessly, a single man is stuck with an unfinished plumbing job and a hole in his floor. This results in a very odd relationship with the woman who lives below him. Combining deadpan humor with an austere view of loneliness and a couple of unexpected musical numbers, Tsai Ming-Liang crafted one of the most original films of the 1990s. Produced for French television's 2000 Seen by... series, this was originally broadcast in a 69-minute version called Last Dance. This longer version is the director's preferred cut.

35mm print courtesy of Big World Pictures

event.title: <show-title>Eyes Wide Shut</show-title>
event.headline: Cruise and Kidman ask, "Why did I get married?" in Kubrick's chilly final opus
event.description:
"This pot is making you aggressive."

Y’all ready for this? Winter is upon us; it’s theoretically supposed to be getting colder, and cuffing season is well underway. It’s the perfect time to watch EYES WIDE SHUT, Stanley Kubrick’s erotic holiday mystery film about how heterosexual marriage is one big spooky lie! That’s right, “cineaphiles,” we’re closing out our 2026 syllabus applying the Queer Film Theory 101 lens to one of the GOATs. The straights are gonna be mad at us!

Dr. Bill Harford (Tom Cruise) and his wife, Alice (Nicole Kidman), seem to have it all: a thriving medical practice, a healthy young daughter, and a fancy-ass New York apartment, but something uncomfortable simmers beneath the surface of their idyllic heterosexual bliss. When Alice reveals a sexy little secret desire, Bill is sent into a tailspin, leading to an odyssey of sexual tourism through the seedy underbelly of New York’s upper crust. For whatever reason, Tom Cruise is exceptionally gifted at portraying a man crumbling under the weight of a masculinity in crisis, and Nicole Kidman shines as a woman who's had it with the trophy wife lifestyle. Featuring an incredible supporting cast including Sydney Pollack, Todd Field, and a cheeky cameo from bisexual icon Alan Cumming, EYES WIDE SHUT is a perfect movie to watch if you want to get in a confusing and convoluted argument with your partner just before the holidays. It will leave you apologizing profusely, but you won't be exactly sure what you’re apologizing for. “Don't you think one of the charms of marriage is that it makes deception a necessity for both parties?”

show.title: Point Blank (1967)
show.headline: Lee Marvin runs roughshod across the West Coast

event.title: <show-title>Point Blank (1967)</show-title>
event.headline: John Boorman and Lee Marvin bring hardboiled noir into the New Wave
event.description:
"You're a pathetic sight, Walker, from where I'm standing. Chasing shadows. You're played out."

BREATHLESS. TOKYO DRIFTER. POINT BLANK. The 1960s saw a shift in crime films, where the grit and grime of American Noir began to blend with the artistic flourishes of New Wave filmmakers. Style became paramount, narratives shifted in psychedelic directions, and for American directors, the Hays Code's restrictions became somewhat more permeable.

Sometimes considered the first American neo-noir, POINT BLANK is a truly strange and thorny piece of cinema. Directed by John Boorman (DELIVERANCE, THE EXORCIST II, EXCALIBUR) and based on the Parker crime novels of Donald E. Westlake, POINT BLANK tells the sensitive story of professional criminal and all-around tough guy, Walker (Lee Marvin), who embarks on a revenge-fueled rampage after being double-crossed and left for dead by his “partner,” Mal (John Vernon). Walker is uniquely fixated on Mal, and not unlike previous Queer Film Theory 101 entry BRANDED TO KILL, the macho man, manly, so-masculine-it-can’t-possibly-be-gay antics that ensue are loaded to the gills with subtext. Bizarre, fractured, and gorgeously rendered, POINT BLANK is a mythic tale of American disillusionment and brutality. A crime film born in a dreamlike liminal reality, a beautiful, emptying world of distrust and loneliness. (Does it sound weird yet?) Deeply influential, POINT BLANK is a must-see film for anyone who loves movies. It’s that important. But enough about its influence; is Angie Dickinson in it being cunty as all hell? You bet she is! Wait, is Archie Bunker (Carroll O’Connor) from All In The Family in this movie? YES! Put on your tailored suit and bring your clandestine briefcase full of secret documents and/or money to our special Noirvember screening of this classic film.

show.title: Little Women (2019)
show.headline: A masterful adaptation from writer/director Greta Gerwig

event.title: <show-title>Little Women (2019)</show-title>
event.headline: Gerwig’s adaptation of a childhood classic is picture perfect for the holidays
event.description:
Little Women is a timeless tale that’s been adapted over and over again, but no one has adapted quite as perfectly as Greta Gerwig. Starring an A-list cast that includes Saoirse Ronan (reunited from LADY BIRD), Florence Pugh (MIDSOMMAR), Emma Watson (HARRY POTTER series), Eliza Scanlen (Sharp Objects), and Timothée Chalamet (CALL ME BY YOUR NAME), Gerwig creates a beautiful story of sisterhood that touches on themes of grief, first loves, and female independence.

The film follows four sisters growing up in Massachusetts during the Civil War, each of them ambitious in their own ways. Saoirse Ronan plays the lead of the film, Jo March, a cunning young woman who dreams of telling stories for a living when she is older. She is often befuddled by her sister Meg (Watson), who desires to one day be a wife; is annoyed by Amy (Pugh), who trails after her like a little puppy; and is enamored with Beth (Scanlen), who is perhaps the kindest of them all.

Gerwig’s LITTLE WOMEN is like a cozy hug on a brisk winter day. A lovely story that brilliantly balances tears with laughs, it’s no wonder it became an instant holiday classic when it was released in theaters seven years ago.

event.description:
About THE KING OF THE FULL MOON NIGHT
2026 | 20 mins.

The king has fallen ill. A young doctor is summoned to his aid in the dead of night. But his only hope of treating this volatile patient is to believe a story that’s getting quite long in the tooth.

About AMERICAN PSYCHO
2000 | 102 mins.

“Look at that subtle off-white coloring. The tasteful thickness of it. Oh, my God. It even has a watermark.”

Before Christian Bale was the savior of Gotham, he was the chainsaw-wielding, business card-slinging scourge of Manhattan. Caught during the height of American Yuppieism in the late '80s, Patrick Bateman finds himself surrounded by friends who he hates and a culture he can’t stand. Can anyone blame him for allowing his nightly bloodlust to overflow into the day?

It’s hard to imagine anyone aside from Bale lecturing a soon-to-be victim on the cultural undertones found within Huey Lewis and The News’ “Hip to be Square,” all while wearing a raincoat and holding an incredibly shiny axe. But, what now seems meant to be almost wasn’t! The role was originally offered to none other than Leonardo DiCaprio. However, due to his newfound fame within the teenaged female demographic, Leo’s managers felt that a stint as a sociopathic mass murderer might somehow taint his image. I guess a career in murders and executions isn’t for everyone.

DCP courtesy of Lionsgate

show.headline: Zombies, guns and sex, oh my!

event.title: <show-title>Cemetery Man</show-title> <event-type-title>4K Restoration</event-type-title>
event.headline: Demented Italian fantasy/horror, newly restored via Severin Films.
event.description:
Francesco Dellamorte (Rupert Everett) is the groundskeeper at a cemetery where the dead just won't stay dead – and it's up to him to deal with those who come back to life with a hunger for human flesh. But Dellamorte's job soon becomes much more complicated when he falls for an enigmatic young woman (Anna Falchi) whose husband has recently died. Based on the novel by Tiziano Sclavi (DYLAN DOG) and directed by Michele Soavi (THE CHURCH), CEMETERY MAN is a late masterpiece of Italian horror: quirky, gory, romantic, and unlike anything else.

Soavi’s cult classic CEMETERY MAN (DELLAMORTE DELLAMORE), a tribute to the giallo masters with whom he apprenticed, is a vertiginous blend of the high delirium of the Italian genre and a mind-bending meta-product at least 20 years ahead of its time. A zombie film, a sexy romance, a comedy, and at last a tragedy, see this tasteful rarity on the big screen as the gods intended.

New 4K restoration courtesy of Severin Films

show.headline: A bad dream wafting in through an open window - a giallo-adjacent nightmare!

event.title: <show-title>Footprints on the Moon</show-title>
event.headline: A bad dream wafting in through an open window - a giallo-adjacent nightmare!
event.description:
In the most criminally underseen giallo of the ‘70s, Florinda Bolkan (A LIZARD IN A WOMAN’S SKIN, FLAVIA THE HERETIC) masterfully stars as a freelance translator who wakes one morning missing all memory of her past three days. She is also tormented by a nightmare involving Klaus Kinski, who may or may have been in charge of an operation that left astronauts stranded on the moon. But will a trail of odd clues lead her to a place where perception and identity are never what they seem? Will Alice unravel her identity amidst rampant murder and surrealism? Nicoletta Elmi (DEEP RED), Evelyn Stewart (THE SWEET BODY OF DEBORAH), Lila Kedrova (THE TENANT) and Klaus Kinski co-star in this “visually stunning gem” (Mondo Digital) – also known as FOOTPRINTS ON THE MOON – directed by Luigi Bazzoni (THE FIFTH CORD) with cinematography by three-time Oscar winner Vittorio Storaro (THE BIRD WITH THE CRYSTAL PLUMAGE), now scanned in 4K from the original camera negatives.

Restoration courtesy of Severin Films

event.title: <show-title>Henry: Portrait of a Serial Killer</show-title>
event.headline: An unflinching gaze into a serial killer from John McNaughton﻿﻿﻿﻿
event.description:
One of the most harrowing films of the 20th century, HENRY is just as much in conversation with SEX, LIES, AND VIDEOTAPE as it is with THE TEXAS CHAIN SAW MASSACRE or DAWN OF THE DEAD. It’s right up there with key works by Haneke, Cronenberg, and Noé in its effortless ability to push the audience in directions it never thought it’d go. Presaging both our current true-crime obsession and “elevated arthouse horror,” this shockingly audacious debut by John McNaughton (WILD THINGS), with its chilling career-defining turn by Michael Rooker (“The Walking Dead”, GUARDIANS OF THE GALAXY), has inspired multiple generations of filmmakers to go for the throat. (AGFA)

New 4K restoration courtesy of the American Genre Film Archive

About CROCODILE DOSE
2026 | 70 mins.

On their first summer back from college, best friends Curtis (Chase Mackay), Jimmy (Graham Cox), and Abe (Jason Waters) embark on a fantastical 24-hour odyssey of drugs and alcohol on their way to a house party hosted by Curtis’s ex-girlfriend, Jane (Avery Boggs). When their pursuit of hedonism leads to Jane and Curtis reuniting prematurely, Curtis is unable to handle his emotions and loses touch with his relationships and reality.

CROCODILE DOSE is a teen comedy told through cell phones, digital photography, and the internet. Set in a magical Denver, the film explores falling in love and growing up in a technologically interconnected world.

event.headline: The explosive story of an accident that turned into murder!
event.description: Fred and his wife Janet have been experiencing problems in their marriage. But when she refuses to help him fund the building of a rural resort and, subsequently, reveals that she's had an affair, Fred snaps, staging a car accident on a country road and leaving Janet for dead. What seems like a perfect crime, disguised as an accident, is spoiled by the unexpected arrival of Al, an innocent passer-by who, in his attempt to save Janet, quickly finds himself fingered as the most likely suspect in her murder. A riveting and criminally under-seen Hitchcockian thriller, director Brian Damude's SUDDEN FURY arrived on the cusp of Canada's tax shelter era, and it ranks as one of the country's most enduring genre staples.

marketStrings.value: The personal closed captioning device displays feature film dialogue and other audio in the form of English-language text for individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing.

The descriptive audio headset provides individuals who are blind or have low vision with an English-language narration of the details of the feature presentation that can't be understood by the soundtrack alone.

Upon request at the box office, we provide assistive listening headsets with amplified audio for those individuals who are hard of hearing. For guests who prefer to use their own hearing aids, neck loops, or cochlear implants, our assistive listening headsets have a 3.5mm headphone jack to connect to those devices.

In order to ensure the highest quality experience for all guests, you may not enter a movie after it has started. We’d love to see you up to 30 minutes early. Running late? No worries, we will happily exchange your ticket for a different showtime or a raincheck to a future show.
